Consider two sets of $25$ paired observations ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{25},$ and ${y}_{1},{y}_{2},…,{y}_{25}.$ You are given that

$$
\begin{aligned} & {\sum }_{i=1}^{25}{x}_{i}=250,\,{\sum }_{i=1}^{25}{y}_{i}=265, \\  & {\sum }_{i=1}^{25}{x}_{i}^{2}=3\,460,\,{\sum }_{i=1}^{25}{y}_{i}^{2}=5\,720.\end{aligned}
$$

Calculate the sum of the squared deviations from the mean for the points ${x}_{i}.$

${S}_{xx}=$
{{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
Given a set of $n$ paired observations ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ and ${y}_{1},{y}_{2},…,{y}_{n},$ the sum of squared deviations from the mean for the data ${x}_{i}$ can be calculated as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{xx} & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})^{2} \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{2}-\frac{1}{n}{({\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i})}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the given statistics in the above formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{xx} & =3\,460-\frac{1}{25}(250)^{2} \\  & =3\,460-2\,500 \\  & =960.\end{aligned}
$$

Given a set of $n$ paired observations ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ and ${y}_{1},{y}_{2},…,{y}_{n},$ the sum of products of deviations from the means can be calculated as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{xy} & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y}) \\  & ={\sum }_{i}{x}_{i}{y}_{i}-\frac{1}{n}({\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i})({\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{y}_{i})\end{aligned}
$$

First, we calculate the sum of the ${x}_{i}$ and ${y}_{i}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} & =12+4+6+10+8+15+11=66, \\ {\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{y}_{i} & =20+10+5+1+7+4+9=56\end{aligned}
$$

We are given that ${\sum }_{i=1}^{7}{x}_{i}{y}_{i}=535.$

Finally, by substituting in the above formula, we get

$$
{S}_{xy}=535-\frac{1}{7}(66)(56)=535-528=7.
$$

Consider two sets of $40$ paired observations ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{40},$ and ${y}_{1},{y}_{2},…,{y}_{40}.$ You are given that

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{xx}=54,\,{S}_{yy}=35,\,{S}_{xy}=188.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, $Cov(x,y)=$
{{field-1}}.
questions.worked_solution:
Given a set of $n$ paired observations ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ and ${y}_{1},{y}_{2},…,{y}_{n},$ their covariance can be calculated as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Cov(x,y) & =\frac{{S}_{xy}}{n},\end{aligned}
$$

where ${S}_{xy}$ is the sum of products of the deviations of ${x}_{i}$ and ${y}_{i}$ from their means.

We are given that ${S}_{xy}=188.$ Substituting the given statistic in the above formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}Cov(x,y) & =\frac{188}{40} \\  & =4.7.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{yy} & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y})^{2} \\  & ={\sum }_{i}{y}_{i}^{2}-\frac{1}{n}{({\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{y}_{i})}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

First, we calculate the sum of the ${y}_{i}$ data:

$$
{\sum }_{i=1}^{8}{y}_{i}=3+4+5+4+7+2+3+4=32.
$$

We are given that ${\sum }_{i=1}^{8}{y}_{i}^{2}=144.$

Finally, by substituting into the above formula, we get

$$
{S}_{yy}=144-\frac{1}{8}(32)^{2}=144-128=16.
$$
